videos.title: How Solve Intelligence Is Building the Future of AI Patent Law
videos.description:
Solve Intelligence (S23) builds AI software for patent attorneys. More than 700 IP teams use it, including firms like Perkins Coie and DLA Piper and in-house teams at Intel and Siemens. At YC x London, co-founders Chris, Angus, and Sanj sat down with YC Managing Partner Diana Hu to talk about applying to YC with an idea that was two weeks old, reaching millions in revenue with no salesperson and no sales background, and how AI is changing the future of law.

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
videos.description:
A coding agent opens a pull request and picks an email provider for you. How did it choose? Resend co-founder and CEO Zeno Rocha explores answer engine optimization (AEO) through a concrete example: which email provider does Claude Code recommend, and how does that change across model versions? Then comes the agent experience itself. Once the agent picks Resend, can it find the price, set up the account and send its first email?

We also follow an email after the API call succeeds. Zeno explains what happens when Gmail throttles a burst, why a tracking pixel can give you the wrong idea about who opened a message, and how one abusive sender can put other customers’ mail at risk. Then we get into the product decisions: giving an agent 80+ named MCP tools, letting it read pricing in Markdown, and letting it register for a service on its own.

Explore the references
• Zeno’s analysis of what Claude Code recommends: https://x.com/zenorocha/status/2027757871597822022
• Resend’s $3M email safety pledge: https://resend.com/blog/3-million-to-make-email-safer
• React Email, the open-source email components: https://react.email/

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: What Frontier Labs Buy: A Data Deep Dive with Handshake AI — Garrett Lord & Team
videos.description:
Our first deep dive with an AI data company. Handshake AI went from launch to roughly $1 billion in annualized gross revenue in about a year. What are frontier labs actually buying? Garrett Lord and the team open up the reinforcement learning environments behind their expert training data, from biology and investment banking to alignment.

An AI agent found a way to earn credit for net income: open a new Excel tab and fill it with every number from one to a million. The grader found the number it wanted. A banker would have looked for it in the right row, for the right year.

Garrett Lord and the Handshake AI team take Latent Space inside the work of building evaluations for frontier labs. A scientist walks us through a gel and nine brain-tissue slides. A banker follows an agent through its inbox, Python code, and financial model to find the assumption that broke the deal. The safety team shows how to read an agent’s actions when its final answer sounds fine.

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: Will Repos Become Software Factories? — Mihail Eric, Monaco
videos.description:
What do you assign when students can finish last year’s homework with one prompt? For the second run of Stanford’s CS146S, Mihail Eric brought open-source maintainers into the course. Students have to understand an unfamiliar repo, propose a change, and explain it to the person who will review their code.

Mihail teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco. We work through his ten-week syllabus, from watching the tool calls inside Claude Code to deciding what a subagent should return to its parent. At Monaco, his team chose to build its own agent workspaces, buy code review tools, and give an on-call agent access to Datadog and GitHub. Mihail explains the reasoning behind those decisions.

Mihail thinks open-source repos will become agent-run software factories. If the factory can produce a patch, what should a junior engineer be learning to do?
